I farm the way we always do here, looking at what my own land did before and what the neighbors are doing. I cannot read much and I do not sit and calculate fancy things, but I know my fields. On my 8 mu, I will keep most of the land in wheat-maize because that is the steady way to get grain and cash, and I will keep a smaller piece in cotton for extra income. Wheat and maize are safer for the household, and cotton can make money if the year is decent, but cotton needs more watching and picking. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I cannot water too freely. This year I will keep 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 3 mu in cotton. For wheat, since it is already standing from last autumn, I will mainly manage water and one more fertilizer dressing if the leaves look weak. After wheat harvest I will rush to plant maize on that same land, with simple tillage so I do not lose time. Cotton I will plant on the 3 mu around late April. I will not push inputs too hard because cash must be kept in hand, but I also do not want to be too stingy and lose yield.
